chunks: And in another report from him, it was added in (the manuscript) H:

Abu Surah said: That young man asked about my well-being, so I informed him of my financial straits and my family. He continued to accompany me until we reached Nawawis at dawn, so we sat down. Then he dug with his hand, and behold, water emerged. He performed ablution and then prayed thirteen units of prayer. Then he said to me: Go to Abul Hasan Ali ibn Yahya, convey my greetings to him and say to him: The man says to you: Give Abu Surah one hundred dinars from the seven hundred dinars that are buried at such-and-such place. And I went immediately to his house and knocked at the door. He said: Who is this? I said: Tell Abul Hasan: This is Abu Surah. I heard him say: What does Abu Surah have to do with me? Then he came out to me, I greeted him and narrated the story to him. He went inside and brought out to me one hundred dinars, so I took them. He said to me: Did you shake hands with him? I said: Yes. So he took my hand and placed it on his eyes and wiped his face with it.

key_terms.صَافَحْتَهُ: Did you shake hands with him

ai.seo_question: What happened when Abu Surah delivered the money to Ali ibn Yahya from the Imam?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the Imam’s hidden presence and his use of trusted intermediaries like Abu Surah to manage affairs during the Minor Occultation. The specific detail of the Imam placing his hand on Abu Surah’s eyes and face serves as a physical manifestation of *barakah* (blessing) and spiritual connection, reinforcing the reality of the Imam’s continued guidance despite his concealment from public view.
